title: Sparse chunkization and delayed finalization: ensure correct token accounting for partial/late-binding stream fragments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

We observe intermittent discrepancies between provisional token tallies reported during streaming sessions and the final committed charges. Root causes we've identified in preliminary investigation: sparse chunkization (clients sending only delta fragments with implicit context), out-of-order and duplicate fragment delivery, keepalive/zero-token frames that shift watermarks, and a finalization path that currently performs immediate optimistic crediting. Consequences: overcharges (double-counting when fragments replay), undercharges (final fragment lost), and difficult-to-reconcile ledgers leading to customer support tickets and credits.

Goal:
Design and ship a robust finalization protocol for streaming sessions that guarantees deterministic, idempotent, and auditable token accounting across reorders, duplicates, and delayed final fragments while limiting latency and memory overhead.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Introduce per-session provisional crediting and a finalization watermark. Credits added during streaming are marked provisional in the ledger and not counted against long-term quota until session finalizes.
2) Require monotonically increasing fragment_seq_id from clients; server-side checks detect gaps/duplicates. Fragments without seq IDs fall back to best-effort path but are marked higher-risk.
3) Finalization happens when either: a) client sends an explicit FINAL fragment, or b) server-side checkpoint expiry (configurable, default 30s of inactivity) advances the watermark and commits provisional credits.
4) Implement an idempotent commit operation that reconciles provisional -> committed using fragment checksums and sequence windows. Replays should be ignored.
5) Add a background reconciliation job (metering-reconciler) to retroactively repair sessions where final fragments were lost or reordered beyond expiry; this job produces audit entries and issues credits/refunds when needed.
6) Telemetry: expose provisional vs committed token counts per session, pending_finalizations, and finalization_latency metrics.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Provisional credits avoid immediate over or undercharging but increase short-term memory/storage for provisional pools. We will bound this with per-account caps and eviction policies.
- Waiting for explicit finalization reduces ambiguity but can increase perceived latency for charge confirmation; configurable expiry balances correctness and UX.
- Reconciliation job adds complexity but is necessary to heal historical mismatches without blocking live traffic.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
The change is opt-in per model/policy initially. Default behavior for existing customers remains unchanged for two weeks while we monitor pilot accounts. We will then enable by default with a migration window and run reconciliation for the prior 90 days of sessions with flagged anomalies.

Deliverables:
- Protocol changes in serving runtime and API contract updates (explicit fragment_seq_id + optional FINAL flag)
- Provisional ledger schema change (marking credits provisional) and commit API
- Metering-reconciler job and audit sink
- E2E simulator + property-based tests that generate reordered/duplicate fragments
- Dashboards and billing alerting rules
acceptance_criteria: No double-charge observed in synthetic harness for 10k simulated sessions with random reordering and duplication
Provisional token counts exposed in console and matched to committed counts after finalization in >= 99.9% of sessions
Reconciler can detect and repair lost-final-fragment cases and emits audit records for every repaired session
Performance: provisional path adds <2ms p50 latency to stream fragment processing and <1% memory overhead under pilot load
Migration: run reconciliation for 90-day window and publish a report with repair counts and credit totals
subtasks: ENG: runtime - add fragment_seq_id enforcement and provisional credit marker
ENG: ledger - schema migration and commit API (provisional->committed)
ENG: reconciler - implement backfill and repair job with audit log
ENG: qa - build e2e simulator, property-based tests, and long-tail fuzzing harness
PM: pilot rollout plan + customer communication for migration

audit_plan: All provisional -> committed transitions write an immutable audit record with session_id, fragment_seq_range, checksum, provisional_tokens, committed_tokens, operator_id. Reconciler emits repair records with before/after token tallies and customer-impact tags. Audit sink ships to internal BigQuery dataset 'metering_audit.finalizations' and retained for 2 years.
rollback_plan: Feature gated; rollback = flip feature flag to disable provisional path and run fast reconciler to commit or revert provisional credits within the rollback window. For pilot accounts, manual ledger adjustments may be applied if needed.
